newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer says discussed Bre-X offer.
newsitem.headline: Placer says discussed Bre-X offer.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said Monday that it had discussed a "conditional offer" with Bre-X Minerals Ltd well in excess of Bre-X's current market price before those talks were broken off.

Earlier Placer sent a letter to the Indonesian government saying it would like to make an offer for Bre-X and its rich Busang gold discovery in Indonesia. Last week Bre-X said the Indonesian government directed it to strike a deal with Barrick Gold Corp by Wednesday.
"Placer Dome confirms that it remains keen to acquire a substantial interest in Busang and wishes to rapidly develop the property," the company said.

Placer chief executive John Willson said that Placer wrote to the Indonesian government after one of its diplomats was quoted as saying other offers would be considered before Wednesday's deadline. "We were very disappointed to see the auction process pre-empted. We regret that the opportunity for Bre-X shareholders to determine the value of their holdings, and to exercise their natural right to determine their partner, was taken away," Willson said.

A Placer spokesman declined to reveal the price Placer had discussed with Bre-X. "You can take my word for it. It's considerably higher than the current price and for that matter the numbers being bandied around" in the market for the Barrick deal, he said.
He declined to say whether the offer was higher than Bre-X's share price two months ago when the talks began. On October 1, Bre-X stock was at C$26.50. It closed Monday at C$17.75.
Placer has not had a response from the Indonesian government to the letter, mailed late last week. But it hopes for one by Wednesday's deadline, the spokesman said.
